title: How duplicate attribution changes database coverage in two reviews of AI in engineering education
abstract: Which search sources would have recovered all studies retained by a review? The database printed on each accepted row can give a misleading answer when another source supplied a duplicate. We reconstruct the search-source incidences of 22 accepted titles in one education review and three final studies in another. Accounting for duplicates reduces the loss attributed to omitting IEEE from eight titles to one in the first register. Its three sources remain necessary. In the second, the ACM export alone contains all three final studies, while the set of 15 studies advancing to the preceding screening stage requires both ACM and ScienceDirect. A reference marked for inclusion during backward searching resolves to one of the original three. These are retrospective results for frozen search exports. They identify the consequences of attribution and denominator choice for these reviews.
